q: How do I calculate a coal power plant's CO2 per kWh from its heat rate?
title: Coal power: CO2 per kWh from heat rate
short: Multiply the heat rate by the coal's CO2 per unit of energy. A plant at 2,400 kcal per kWh gross, burning coal near 95 kg CO2 per GJ, emits about 0.95 kg CO2 per kWh generated, and about 1.0 per kWh sent out once auxiliary power is taken off.
audience: Captive and utility coal power plants in Chhattisgarh and elsewhere, and units buying captive power from them

ul: kcal per kWh x 4.1868 = kJ per kWh; divide by a million for GJ.
GJ per kWh x kg CO2 per GJ of your coal = kg CO2 per kWh generated.
Divide by (1 minus auxiliary share) for kWh sent out.

p: Indian coal varies widely in ash and energy. A lab measured carbon content or a factor tied to your coal's calorific value beats a single default.
Captive users should report the plant's actual figure, not the grid's 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor). The CEA database also lists station wise figures for utility plants.

example.title: Worked example
lines: 2,400 kcal/kWh x 4.1868 = 10,048 kJ = 0.01005 GJ per kWh
0.01005 GJ x 95 kg CO2/GJ = 0.955 kg CO2 per kWh generated
With 7% auxiliary use: 0.955 / 0.93 = 1.03 kg CO2 per kWh sent out
example.note: Heat rate, coal factor and auxiliary share are assumptions for illustration.
